author_claim: Paul transposes word order of ἐπίστευσεν and Ἀβραάμ between Rom 4:3 and Gal 3:6 without altering fundamental sense.
short_quote: the words ἐπίστευσεν and Ἀβραάμ have been transposed. The variations in the last two examples do not affect the sense of the texts
qualification: Word-order variation does not affect underlying semantic sense.

author_claim: Paul uses the narrative sequence of Gen 15:6 in Rom 4:3 to support righteousness by faith prior to circumcision.
short_quote: Paul's emphasis on the literary sequence of the Genesis narrative has enabled him to use scripture to support his distinction between righteousness by faith and circumcision
qualification: Paul believed he was uncovering the intrinsic meaning of the text.

author_claim: Paul follows LXX-B tradition using forms of ἀγαπάω rather than LXX-A which reads forms of ἐλεέω.
short_quote: Paul and LXX-B have forms of ἀγαπᾶν, whereas LXX-A uses forms of ἐλεεῖν
notes: Visibly verified on thesis p. 69 n. 19.

author_claim: Paul substitutes καλέσω for ἐρῶ in Hos 2:23 to create a verbal connection with κληθήσονται in Hos 1:10 and Rom 9:24.
short_quote: The substitution of καλέσω for ἐρῶ in the citation from Hosea 2:25 LXX, has resulted in a verbal connection in Paul's text between the two Hosea passages
source_locator: Chapter VI, p. 178; cf. Chapter III, p. 81 (PDF pp. 188, 91)
qualification: Framed as probable motivation for modification.
notes: Visibly verified on thesis p. 178; cf. p. 81.

author_claim: Paul's text in Rom 9:26 exhibits direct textual agreement with Codex Alexandrinus (LXX-A) in Hos 1:10.
notes: Visibly verified on thesis pp. 69–70 n. 19.

author_claim: The phrase υἱοὶ θεοῦ ζῶντος in Hos 1:10 functions as a verbal link with υἱῶν Ἰσραήλ in Isa 10:22 (Rom 9:27).
short_quote: The verbal link is between υἱοὶ θεοῦ ζῶντος in 9:26 and υἱῶν Ἰσραήλ in 9:27

author_claim: Paul's inclusion of ἐπʼ αὐτῷ in Rom 10:11 aligns with Codex Alexandrinus (LXX-A) against Codex Vaticanus (LXX-B).
short_quote: ἐπʼ αὐτῷ included in Paul and LXX-A, but omitted in LXX-B); 10:11 (same as 9:33)
notes: Visibly verified on thesis p. 69 n. 19.

author_claim: Paul probably inserted πᾶς into Isa 28:16 in Rom 10:11 due to catchword association with πᾶς in Joel 2:32 (Rom 10:13).
short_quote: In the second of these references, he inserts the word πᾶς. This addition probably came about as a result of the association of Isaiah 28:16 with Joel
source_locator: Chapter III, p. 83; cf. Chapter VI, p. 183 (PDF pp. 93, 193)
notes: Visibly verified on thesis p. 83; cf. p. 183.

author_claim: Paul cites Joel 2:32 in Rom 10:13 using catchwords πᾶς and ἐπικαλέομαι to argue universal salvation for Jews and Greeks.
short_quote: The two words, πᾶς and ἐπικαλέσασθαι are key words for Paul, and they assist him in developing an argument concerning the salvation of both Jews and Greeks

author_claim: Paul's word order σύμβουλος αὐτοῦ in Rom 11:34 follows LXX-A, whereas LXX-B transposes to αὐτοῦ σύμβουλος.
short_quote: Paul and LXX-A read σύμβουλος αὐτοῦ, but LXX-B transposes the terms
notes: Visibly verified on thesis p. 69 n. 19.

author_claim: Paul quotes different clauses of Isa 40:13 in Rom 11:34 and 1 Cor 2:16 to serve distinct epistolary contexts.
short_quote: the two citations from Isaiah 40:13 illustrate the way in which Paul has used different forms of the same passage

author_claim: Paul quotes Isa 11:10 in Rom 15:12 within a catena linked by catchword ἔθνη to substantiate Gentile hope and election.
short_quote: Note the verbal connection between the scriptural passages and the opening statement centring on the word ἔθνη
qualification: Omission of ἐν τῇ ἡμέρᾳ ἐκείνῃ is stylistic (pp. 74–76).
notes: Visibly verified on thesis p. 91 n. 16.

author_claim: Paul cites Isa 29:14 in 1 Cor 1:19 as a verbal catalyst generating the ensuing discussion on human wisdom vs cross.
short_quote: the scriptural citation is related not only to the opening statement but also contributes thematically and verbally to the discussion that follows

author_claim: Within the shared core quotation (ἔσονται οἱ δύο εἰς σάρκα μίαν), Paul's only difference in Gen 2:24 between 1 Cor 6:16 and Eph 5:31 is the introductory formula γάρ, φησίν added for syntax; Eph 5:31 serves as an outside-primary-corpus comparator.
short_quote: the only difference between the two references is that the introductory formula, γάρ, φησίν, has been included for syntactical reasons
qualification: Aageson's evaluation applies strictly to shared core clause (ἔσονται οἱ δύο εἰς σάρκα μίαν); full citation in Eph 5:31 includes preceding clause omitted in 1 Cor 6:16. Per PROJECT_CONSTITUTION.md, Ephesians is categorized strictly as an outside-primary-corpus comparator.
notes: Visibly verified on thesis pp. 82–83; core clause comparison distinguishes author claim from full manuscript text.

author_claim: Paul applies Gen 2:24 in 1 Cor 6:16 halakically to govern sexual ethics, deriving behavioral instruction from narrative.
short_quote: In four instances, "narrative" passages are used in contexts which pertain to ethics; [n. 120: I Cor. 6:16 (Gen. 2:24)...]
notes: Visibly verified on thesis p. 114 n. 120.

author_claim: Paul cites Deut 25:4 in 1 Cor 9:9 with variant κημώσεις and applies it διʼ ἡμᾶς to apostolic right to material support.
short_quote: The context of this statement in I Corinthians concerns Paul's apostolic right to receive material support, and it is to this situation that Paul has applied the scriptural citation
qualification: Notes recognized Greek MS variant κημώσεις/φιμώσεις (p. 68 n. 15).

author_claim: Paul cites Exod 32:6 in 1 Cor 10:7 as a midrashic parenetic warning (τύπος) against idolatry, not formal typology.
short_quote: the use of τύπος and τυπικῶς in the sense of 'warning' or 'example' in I Corinthians 10:6-13 provides little support for the view that Paul's use of scripture is fundamentally typological
qualification: Distinguishes parenetic warning from redemptive typology.

author_claim: Paul or tradition omits ὑπὸ θεοῦ from Deut 21:23 in Gal 3:13 to avoid presenting an unacceptable image of the divine.
short_quote: his text omits the words ὑπὸ θεοῦ... likely that they were omitted in order to avoid presenting an unacceptable image of the divine
qualification: Cannot prove whether Paul or tradition initiated omission.
